### Steps to reproduce issue

1. Create a simple publisher as explained in the [official tutorial](https://docs.ros.org/en/jazzy/Tutorials/Beginner-Client-Libraries/Writing-A-Simple-Py-Publisher-And-Subscriber.html).
2. Modify the `qos_profile` of the publisher node as follows
  ```python
  from rclpy.qos import LivelinessPolicy, QoSProfile
  qos_profile = QoSProfile(depth=10, liveliness=LivelinessPolicy.BEST_AVAILABLE)
  self.publisher_ = self.create_publisher(String, 'topic', qos_profile)
  ```
3. Modify the `qos_profile` of the subscriber node as follows
  ```python
  from rclpy.qos import LivelinessPolicy, QoSProfile
  qos_profile = QoSProfile(depth=10, liveliness=LivelinessPolicy.BEST_AVAILABLE)
  self.subscription = self.create_subscription(
      String,
      'topic',
      self.listener_callback,
      qos_profile)
    self.subscription  # prevent unused variable warning
  ```
4. open a terminal run the publisher node
  ```sh
  source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
  colcon build --packages-select ros_experiments --symlink-install
  source install/setup.bash
  ros2 run ros_experiments test_publisher
  ```
5. in another terminal check the publisher liveliness:
  ```sh
  source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
  ros2 topic info /topic --verbose
  ```
6. in yet another terminal run the subscriber node
  ```sh
  source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
  source install/setup.bash
  ros2 run ros_experiments test_subscriber
  ```

### Expected behavior

I would expect the liveliness to be `BEST_AVAILABLE` but it is still `AUTOMATIC`. Moreover I would expect that, since the same QoS profile is applied to both publisher and subscriber, they would be compatible.

### Actual behavior

The liveliness still shows as `AUTOMATIC`.

```sh
$ ros2 topic info /topic --verbose
Type: std_msgs/msg/String

Publisher count: 1

Node name: minimal_publisher
Node namespace: /
Topic type: std_msgs/msg/String
Topic type hash: RIHS01_df668c740482bbd48fb39d76a70dfd4bd59db1288021743503259e948f6b1a18
Endpoint type: PUBLISHER
GID: 01.0f.7d.17.95.6b.b2.2f.00.00.00.00.00.00.13.03
QoS profile:
  Reliability: RELIABLE
  History (Depth): UNKNOWN
  Durability: VOLATILE
  Lifespan: Infinite
  Deadline: Infinite
  Liveliness: AUTOMATIC
  Liveliness lease duration: Infinite

Subscription count: 0
```

Moreover the subscriber cannot subscribe to the publisher and complains about incompatible QoS.
```sh
$ ros2 run ros_experiments test_subscriber
[WARN] [1756348112.598568447] [minimal_subscriber]: New publisher discovered on topic 'topic', offering incompatible QoS. No messages will be received from it. Last incompatible policy: LIVELINESS
```

### Additional information

It might be that the "best available" liveliness is actually `AUTOMATIC`, but in such a case I would expect to see something like `AUTOMATIC (best available)` in the output of the `ros2 topic info /topic --verbose` command. But more importantly, I would expect the subscriber to subscribe without complaining.

This is a minor issue, so please feel free to close this report if you think that it is too low priority.

I am attaching a zip file with the test environment if you want to reproduce this.

[ros_experiments.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22016662/ros_experiments.zip)

Steps to reproduce issue

  1. Create a simple publisher as explained in the official tutorial.
  2. Modify the qos_profile of the publisher node as follows
from rclpy.qos import LivelinessPolicy, QoSProfile
qos_profile = QoSProfile(depth=10, liveliness=LivelinessPolicy.BEST_AVAILABLE)
self.publisher_ = self.create_publisher(String, 'topic', qos_profile)
  1. Modify the qos_profile of the subscriber node as follows
from rclpy.qos import LivelinessPolicy, QoSProfile
qos_profile = QoSProfile(depth=10, liveliness=LivelinessPolicy.BEST_AVAILABLE)
self.subscription = self.create_subscription(
    String,
    'topic',
    self.listener_callback,
    qos_profile)
  self.subscription  # prevent unused variable warning
  1. open a terminal run the publisher node
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
colcon build --packages-select ros_experiments --symlink-install
source install/setup.bash
ros2 run ros_experiments test_publisher
  1. in another terminal check the publisher liveliness:
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
ros2 topic info /topic --verbose
  1. in yet another terminal run the subscriber node
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source install/setup.bash
ros2 run ros_experiments test_subscriber

Expected behavior

I would expect the liveliness to be BEST_AVAILABLE but it is still AUTOMATIC. Moreover I would expect that, since the same QoS profile is applied to both publisher and subscriber, they would be compatible.

Actual behavior

The liveliness still shows as AUTOMATIC.

$ ros2 topic info /topic --verbose
Type: std_msgs/msg/String

Publisher count: 1

Node name: minimal_publisher
Node namespace: /
Topic type: std_msgs/msg/String
Topic type hash: RIHS01_df668c740482bbd48fb39d76a70dfd4bd59db1288021743503259e948f6b1a18
Endpoint type: PUBLISHER
GID: 01.0f.7d.17.95.6b.b2.2f.00.00.00.00.00.00.13.03
QoS profile:
  Reliability: RELIABLE
  History (Depth): UNKNOWN
  Durability: VOLATILE
  Lifespan: Infinite
  Deadline: Infinite
  Liveliness: AUTOMATIC
  Liveliness lease duration: Infinite

Subscription count: 0

Moreover the subscriber cannot subscribe to the publisher and complains about incompatible QoS.

$ ros2 run ros_experiments test_subscriber
[WARN] [1756348112.598568447] [minimal_subscriber]: New publisher discovered on topic 'topic', offering incompatible QoS. No messages will be received from it. Last incompatible policy: LIVELINESS

Additional information

It might be that the "best available" liveliness is actually AUTOMATIC, but in such a case I would expect to see something like AUTOMATIC (best available) in the output of the ros2 topic info /topic --verbose command. But more importantly, I would expect the subscriber to subscribe without complaining.

This is a minor issue, so please feel free to close this report if you think that it is too low priority.

I am attaching a zip file with the test environment if you want to reproduce this.

ros_experiments.zip

commit.message:
rclpy: Resolve invalid use of LivelinessPolicy.BEST_AVAILABLE by mapping to AUTOMATIC

The Python QoS API exposes , but the underlying
rmw layer does not define or support a “best available” liveliness enum value.
As a result, rclpy forwarded the raw enum value (5) into rmw_qos_profile_t,
leading to inconsistent behavior:

-  reports liveliness as AUTOMATIC
- rclpy_qos_check_compatible reports LIVELINESS incompatibility
- publisher and subscription using identical QoS settings cannot communicate

This patch resolves the inconsistency by explicitly mapping
 to  when building
the rmw QoS profile. This matches how the best_available preset QoS profile is
defined in rmw, and restores compatibility between endpoints.

A deprecation warning may be added in a future release to clarify that
BEST_AVAILABLE for liveliness is not a standalone rmw policy.

Fixes: ros2/ros2#1722

The Python QoS API exposes , but the underlying
rmw layer does not define or support a “best available” liveliness enum value.
As a result, rclpy forwarded the raw enum value (5) into rmw_qos_profile_t,
leading to inconsistent behavior:

-  reports liveliness as AUTOMATIC
- rclpy_qos_check_compatible reports LIVELINESS incompatibility
- publisher and subscription using identical QoS settings cannot communicate

This patch resolves the inconsistency by explicitly mapping
 to  when building
the rmw QoS profile. This matches how the best_available preset QoS profile is
defined in rmw, and restores compatibility between endpoints.

A deprecation warning may be added in a future release to clarify that
BEST_AVAILABLE for liveliness is not a standalone rmw policy.

Fixes: ros2/ros2#1722
Signed-off-by: pavansai018 <18pavansai@gmail.com>

@fujitatomoya 

Sorry for the late reply. I confirmed that the error.

```log
[WARN] [1756348112.598568447] [minimal_subscriber]: New publisher discovered on topic 'topic', offering incompatible QoS. No messages will be received from it. Last incompatible policy: LIVELINESS
```
is fixed in the latest version of the [rmw_dds_common](https://github.com/ros2/rmw_dds_common) package (6.0.0) but still present in the latest public version (4.0.2).

Thank you for the fix.
